sourceIssues.printed: "Corollary 1.1.15. Let G be an arbitrary connected reductive group over Q_p with a Q_p-rational Levi subgroup M. Let μ: G_m → M be a minuscule cocharacter and [b_M] ∈ B(M)_b such that ([b_M], {μ}) is G-admissible. Then there exists w ∈ W(G, M) := N_G(M)/M such that ([b_M], {w·μ}) is M-admissible." Proof: "(1.1.13) implies that there exists w* ∈ W(G*, M*) such that ([b_{M*}], {w*·μ*}) is M*-admissible."
sourceIssues.correction: Use the absolute geometric Weyl group W(G,T) for a maximal torus T of M containing a representative of μ, with compatible choices under the inner twisting, rather than N_G(M)/M. Equivalently, some G(Q̄_p)-conjugate μ′ of μ factoring through T makes ([b_M], {μ′}) M-admissible. No Q_p-rationality of μ or of a chosen Weyl representative is asserted.
sourceIssues.reason: The printed statement fails already for split G. Take G = GL_3, M = GL_1 × GL_2 (blocks of sizes 1 and 2), μ = (0,1,0) and b_M = diag(p,1,1), which is basic in M. Then ([b_M], {μ}) is G-admissible: its Newton point (1,0,0) equals the dominant μ̄, and both have κ_G = 1. But κ_M(b_M) = (1,0), while κ_M(μ) = (0,1). Since the blocks have different sizes, N_G(M) = M, so W(G, M) is trivial and no w in it helps. The permutation of the first two coordinates, in W(G, T) = S_3, does. The proof transports to the quasi-split inner form and applies Proposition 1.1.13. That proposition gives w* in the absolute Weyl group W(G*, T*), not in N_{G*}(M*)/M*, so the proof establishes the corrected statement. The only use is in the proof of Corollary 1.1.17, p.13, for G not necessarily quasi-split. It cites "Lemma 1.1.13" (the quasi-split Proposition 1.1.13) in the form w ∈ W(G, T). The corrected Corollary 1.1.15 is exactly what that step needs, so this particular downstream step is repaired; this is not a verification of every later result. Checked on the page images. Noted by the extraction (source discrepancy 2, items N29 and N32), which also verified the Weyl-group computation by machine.

sourceIssues.printed: "Let G′ = G × T, equipped with the symplectic representation V′ = V ⊕ V. Let X′ = X × {h_T}. Then we have (G′, X′) ↪ (G_{V′}, H_{V′}). … Restricting the action of I_{s′_0} to A_T induces a map of Q-groups I_{s′_0} → T, and we consider the composite I_{s′_0} → T → G^ab. By Corollary 2.1.9, I_{s′_0} → I_{s_0} is surjective, so the map I_{s′_0} → G^ab factors through I_{s_0}, as this is true over Q_ℓ for any ℓ ≠ p."
sourceIssues.correction: Replace G′=G×T by H=G×_{G^ab}T. This is a connected reductive central-torus extension of G, with kernel 1×(T∩G^der). The similitude character factors through G^ab, so the two blocks have equal multipliers; h^ab is constant on X, so X×{h_T} factors through H. Once the lifted point and compatible I-group maps have been constructed, use C_H((γ,t))=C_G(γ)×_{G^ab}T: projection is a base change of the surjective morphism T→G^ab, with kernel 1×(T∩G^der). Corollary 2.1.9 then gives surjectivity on I-groups over Q_ℓ for ℓ≠p. The composite through T to G^ab kills that kernel, and this descends faithfully flatly to Q. Surjectivity here means a morphism of algebraic groups, not necessarily surjectivity on rational points. The argument must establish kernel triviality, not infer factorization from surjectivity alone.
sourceIssues.reason: The direct-product construction is false as written, not merely an unexplained descent: already for G=GSp_2 and a CM maximal torus T, (1,2·1)∈G×T scales the two blocks of ψ⊕ψ by 1 and 4. Thus it is not a symplectic similitude. Independently of that failed Shimura construction, on the proposed direct-product group the composite G×T→T→G^ab is nontrivial on the kernel 1×T of projection to G, so it cannot descend. The original errata's unconditional claim about I_{s′} is replaced by this group-level obstruction, since the proposed Shimura embedding has already failed. The earlier checkpoint justified centralizer surjectivity by a general central-extension assertion which is false: for GL₂→PGL₂, d=diag(1,−1) and the coordinate swap w satisfy wdw⁻¹=−d, so [w] centralizes [d], but no scalar multiple of w centralizes d. The repaired fibre product has a stronger, direct argument. Since T is commutative, (g,u) commutes with (γ,t) precisely when g commutes with γ. This proves C_H((γ,t))=C_G(γ)×_{G^ab}T as group schemes, giving the asserted surjectivity and kernel without a general semisimple-centralizer claim. Corollary 2.1.9 then gives surjectivity on the I-groups; over Q_ℓ the kernel is killed by T→G^ab, hence over Q as well. Read Lemma 2.2.8, Corollary 2.1.9 and the preceding lifting construction. This repairs the identified local construction/descent; it is not a global certification of Proposition 2.2.2, whose preceding construction has the related E13 defect.

sourceIssues.reason: Independently checked the local obstruction for the quaternion division algebra D/Q_p. Over L, identify D× with GL₂ with Frobenius σ_D=Int(J)σ, J=[[0,p],[1,0]]. The bijection [b]_G↦[bJ]_GL₂ shifts κ by 1 and both Newton slopes by 1/2: the adjoint Frobenius actions agree and the determinant valuations differ by 1. For μ_m=(m+1,m), an ordinary class would therefore yield two distinct rank-one GL₂ isocrystals of slopes m+3/2 and m+1/2, impossible since rank-one slopes are integral. Admissibility confines the GL₂ slopes to [m+1/2,m+3/2], with sum 2m+2. Distinct slopes would each be integral, but the only integer in that interval is m+1. Thus the sole possible Newton vector is (m+1,m+1), realized by b=p^m J, for which bJ=p^(m+1)1. The G-vector is (m+1/2,m+1/2), strictly below μ_m. Taking m=−1 handles an inverse-Hodge representative (0,−1). Kisin–Zhou v2 Definition 2.2.4 and Remark 2.2.5 explicitly state the same existence restriction. This disproves the universal local assertion as printed, not a fully specified global integral-model example or the entire density corollary.

This can be strict within the stated Hodge-type setting: take the CM elliptic curve y²=x³−x with CM by Q(i), its torus Shimura datum T=Res_{Q(i)/Q} G_m, and p=5. Its discriminant is a 5-adic unit; direct counting gives #E(F_5)=8 and trace −2, so its two crystalline slopes are 0 and 1. On a geometric component of the zero-dimensional special fibre, the isocrystal is 1⊕L(1), up to the dual convention, where L(1) denotes the rank-one slope-one object. Its full generated Tannakian category, after extension of scalars to L, is Rep_L G_m: the unit has no independent character and all other objects are sums of integral Tate powers. The stabilizer of the CM Hodge tensors is instead T_L≅G_m², of dimension two. Thus the printed equivalence is false, not merely unjustified; kind is changed from gap to error affecting the proof. This does not disprove the final exact faithful tensor-functor statement: restriction along G_m→G_m² can be exact and faithful without being full.

sourceIssues.correction: The block-diagonal map into GSp(V⊕V′,ψ⊕ψ′) additionally requires equality of the two similitude characters. Replace the group by the identity component of the subgroup of G′×_{G^ad}G cut out by c′(g′)=c(g). The paired Hodge homomorphism has equal multipliers and factors through this subgroup. Recheck the subsequent lifting and centralizer arguments for this corrected group; the present checkpoint establishes the missing condition, not the full repaired proposition. The related construction in Kisin–Zhou arXiv:2103.09945v2 §4.3.7, p.40, explicitly uses (G₂×_{G^ad,G_m}G)^0. Its Proposition 4.4.10, p.45, checks the projection maps using product projectors, central kernels and Frobenius centralizers. Those results have additional integral-model hypotheses; they are evidence for the repair strategy, not a completed verification of this proposition in its full generality. For the centralizer step, first use a common sufficiently divisible Frobenius power as in §2.1.5 and Corollary 2.1.9, pp.22–24. Its cyclic Zariski closure is a torus, so the relevant centralizers are connected Levi subgroups. The corrected group has central surjective projections; over an algebraic closure the projections identify root groups and carry maximal tori onto maximal tori. Corresponding roots have the same value on compatible Frobenius elements, so the roots taking value 1 agree. The restricted centralizer maps are therefore surjective with the same central kernels. This verifies the geometric centralizer step conditional on the compatible lifted points and I-group morphisms; it does not by itself establish their construction, the rational center embeddings, or the quotient assertions.
sourceIssues.reason: The fibre product over the adjoint group does not identify the central multipliers, and taking its identity component does not fix this. Test G′=G=GSp_2=GL_2 with the same Siegel datum and standard representation. The curve a↦(a·1,1) lies in the identity component of the fibre product over PGL_2. At a=2 its block-diagonal action scales ψ′ by 4 and ψ by 1, so it is not a similitude of their direct sum. These data satisfy the accommodating type-C setup (standard two-dimensional representation, with no proper nonzero invariant subspace). Hence the asserted embedding fails even in this basic allowed case. The equality-of-multipliers subgroup removes the obstruction; this is distinct from E5, where equality in all of G^ab is needed for descent. Independently read §2.2.7 pp.26–28 and the p.27 image. E13 avoids reusing E8–E12, which already identify different findings in the newer extraction. The GL₂→PGL₂ counterexample explained under E5 shows why arbitrary semisimple centralizers cannot replace the connected centralizers used in §2.1.5. For the corrected common-multiplier subgroup, each projection is surjective: first lift the adjoint image, then adjust the other component by a scalar to equalize multipliers over an algebraic closure. Taking the identity component preserves surjectivity onto the connected target. The kernels are central, since an element projecting to the identity has trivial image in the other adjoint group. These are statements about algebraic groups, not about surjectivity on Q-points.
